old_definition: A device or instrument, especially of war; also skill, ingenuity or contrivance
modern_definition: A machine that converts energy into motion
notes: From any clever device or war machine to specific power source

old_definition: A scheme, plot, or contrivance; a structure or fabric
modern_definition: A mechanical apparatus or device
notes: From abstract 'scheme' or 'plot' to physical machine

old_definition: An emblem, impresa, or motto; a plan or stratagem
modern_definition: A machine, tool, or electronic gadget
notes: From symbolic emblem or clever plan to physical/electronic tool

old_definition: One who designs or constructs engines or works of fortification
modern_definition: A person who designs, builds, or maintains engines, machines, or systems
notes: Originally military/fortification specialist

old_definition: Knowledge, learning, or skill in any art or discipline
modern_definition: Systematic study of the structure and behavior of the physical and natural world through observation and experiment
notes: From general 'knowledge/skill' to specific empirical method

old_definition: Experience, trial, or proof by testing; a practical test
modern_definition: A scientific procedure undertaken to make a discovery, test a hypothesis, or demonstrate a known fact
notes: From personal trial/experience to formal controlled scientific method

old_definition: The act of watching, noting, or remarking; a remark or comment
modern_definition: The action or process of observing something or someone carefully in order to gain information
notes: Became central method of the Scientific Revolution

old_definition: The act of revealing or disclosing something hidden or unknown
modern_definition: The act of finding or encountering something new, especially for the first time
notes: From 'uncovering what was hidden' to 'finding something new'

old_definition: The act of finding or contriving something; a scheme, device, or discovery
modern_definition: A new device, method, or process created by human ingenuity
notes: Strong shift toward mechanical and technological creation

old_definition: A supposition or proposed explanation to be tested by further investigation
modern_definition: A proposed explanation made on the basis of limited evidence as a starting point for further investigation
notes: Became central to the scientific method

old_definition: A contemplation, speculation, or mental scheme; a set of principles
modern_definition: A system of ideas intended to explain something, especially one based on general principles
notes: From speculation to systematic scientific explanation

old_definition: A person who performs mathematical calculations, especially one employed to do so
modern_definition: An electronic device that stores and processes data according to a set of instructions
notes: Human job title → electronic machine (major 20th century shift)

old_definition: To count, calculate, or compute a sum or total
modern_definition: To think or suppose something; to consider
notes: Classic shift from calculation to casual thinking

old_definition: To reckon or calculate a number or result
modern_definition: To calculate or process data using a computer
notes: From manual arithmetic to electronic computation

old_definition: To do arithmetic or calculate; also zero or a secret code
modern_definition: A secret code or the mathematical symbol for zero
notes: From 'do arithmetic' to 'secret code'

old_definition: A step-by-step procedure for calculation (from Arabic 'al-Khwarizmi')
modern_definition: A set of rules or procedures for solving a problem, especially in computing and mathematics
notes: From medieval mathematical procedure to core computing concept

old_definition: Things that are given or granted; facts or information
modern_definition: Facts and statistics collected together for reference or analysis, especially in computing
notes: From general 'facts' to digital information processed by computers

old_definition: A public notice or proclamation; a plan or schedule
modern_definition: A series of coded instructions that tell a computer what to do
notes: From public notice/plan to computer instructions

old_definition: A string, wire, or folder for keeping papers in order; a tool for smoothing
modern_definition: A collection of data or information stored under a single name on a computer
notes: From physical folder/tool to digital data container

old_definition: The faculty of remembering; remembrance or recollection
modern_definition: The part of a computer where data and instructions are stored for quick access
notes: From human mental faculty to computer hardware component

old_definition: A written account or document; the act of recording
modern_definition: Data stored in a computer system; a vinyl disc for music
notes: From written document to digital data or audio medium

old_definition: A printing press; the act or business of printing books or newspapers
modern_definition: A machine for printing; to push or apply pressure; news media ('the press')
notes: From printing press to apply pressure + news media

old_definition: An optical instrument for viewing distant objects (early term: perspective glass)
modern_definition: An optical instrument designed to make distant objects appear nearer and larger
notes: Word coined in 1611; technology itself is new in this period

old_definition: A magnifying glass or instrument for viewing very small objects
modern_definition: An optical instrument used for viewing very small objects
notes: Early versions called magnifying glasses

old_definition: An optical instrument or glass for seeing objects at a distance
modern_definition: A particular attitude, point of view, or way of regarding something
notes: Physical optical device to abstract viewpoint

old_definition: A number of cannon or heavy guns placed together for action; a fortified emplacement
modern_definition: A device that converts chemical energy into electrical energy; a series of similar units
notes: From cannons to electrical device

old_definition: A storehouse for arms, ammunition, or provisions; a military depot
modern_definition: A periodical publication containing articles, stories, etc.; a storage place for ammunition
notes: From military storehouse to periodical publication

old_definition: One of the four classical substances (earth, air, fire, water); a basic constituent or principle
modern_definition: A substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means; a component
notes: From four elements theory to periodic table elements

old_definition: A preparation in alchemy supposed to prolong life indefinitely or transmute base metals into gold
modern_definition: A medicinal preparation, usually sweetened; a cure-all or panacea
notes: From alchemical life-prolonging potion to modern medicine/syrup

old_definition: A small portable timepiece carried in the pocket; also to keep guard or watch over
modern_definition: A timepiece worn on the wrist; to look at or observe carefully
notes: From pocket watch + 'keep guard' to wristwatch + 'observe'

old_definition: The face of a clock or sundial; a plate marked with divisions
modern_definition: The face of a clock, gauge, or meter; a control on a device
notes: Extended from clock face to any gauge or control
